To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
endogenously-secreted human growth hormone (hGH) modulates the secretion of pituitary gonadotropins and prolactin in young and old female and male transgenetic mice expressing the hGh gene.
endogenously-secreted hGH affects the regulation of gonadal function in young and old female and male transgenics.
the transgenic mice expressing hGH gene are hypogonadal, hypoprolactemic, and hypophyseotropic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of endogenous human growth hormone (hGH) on hypothalamic-piuitary function in transgenic mice expressing human growth hormone (tg-mice).
the role of the growth hormone (GH)-IGF-I axis in the control of reproductive function.
understanding how aging affects the regulation of the reproductive system and how the reproductive system responds to aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of hGH on the reproductive system in the transgenic mice are similar to those reported for humans, and that the effects of aging are similar to those in normal mice.
the endogenously produced hGH in transgenic mice bearing hGH gene is responsible for the age-related changes in the hypothalamus-pituitary axis.
hGH is a modulator of gonadotrophin secretion and that its secretion in the aged is a major factor in the reduction of gonadotrophic secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transgenic mice bearing hGH gene are a good model to study age-related changes in the hypothalamo-pituitary axis.
the transgenic mice bearing hGH gene are a useful model for studying age-related changes in the regulation of gonadal function.
the transgenic mouse model of human growth hormone gene over-expression provides an excellent model of aging in the mouse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endogenously produced GH in transgenic mice is capable of altering the secretion of gonadotrophins and prolactin.
the transgenic animals have an increased life span and are resistant to age-related diseases.
the transgenic mice expressing hGH gene are hypogonadal.
